title: Hygiene Practices in Regional Anaesthesia – An International Cross-Sectional Survey among Anaesthesiologists
summary:
Regional anaesthesia is a commonly used technique in anaesthesia in which specific nerves are numbed. Hygiene measures are essential in this context to prevent infections and ensure patient safety.

However, hygiene standards and their implementation in daily clinical practice vary across countries and healthcare institutions. Currently, there are no unified European recommendations.

The aim of this study is to collect information on current hygiene practices using an anonymous online survey. Anaesthesiologists from different countries are invited to participate.

The results will help identify common practices and differences and may contribute to the development of future recommendations.

interventions.name: Anaesthesiologists participating in an anonymous online survey on hygiene practices in regional anaesthesia.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Medical practice in the field of anaesthesia
Clinical experience in performing or supervising regional anaesthesia procedures
Voluntary participation in the anonymous online survey
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of consent to participate
Incomplete questionnaire (relevant items for analysis not completed)
